subject: Clarify: default capture for interactive vs final outputs and erase request workflow
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <sec@brightbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on what you retain by default (interactive sessions vs final outputs)

Hi Ben,

Quick follow-up from our security review: we need crystal-clear answers on what Redwood keeps by default for hosted API customers. Specifically:
- During interactive sessions (live streaming tokens and partial responses), do you persist incomplete buffers anywhere?
- Do you treat raw customer prompts differently from model-generated outputs for retention?
- If we file an erasure request for a set of user queries, what evidence will you provide that the data was deleted (and what is the SLA)?

We also saw references to KV cache and "derived artifacts" in the docs; please explain persistence behavior for those.

Thanks,
Jane Dow
Product Security, BrightBank

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: BrightBank Security <sec@brightbank.com>, BrightBank PM <jane.dow@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on what you retain by default (interactive sessions vs final outputs)

Jane — thank you for the clear list. I wanted to respond with a concise, customer-facing summary and then add the operational detail below. Short answers first, then specifics you can hand to your auditors.

TL;DR (customer-facing summary):
- Interactive token buffers that are not finalized (streaming fragments) are ephemeral and are not persisted beyond short-lived buffers; default lifetime is 24 hours and they are trimmed automatically unless explicitly captured.
- Finalized prompts (the full request payload once the client signals "end of input") are treated as request records and retained by default for 30 days (hosted API baseline) unless a customer enables stricter residency/auto-delete settings.
- Model outputs (final responses) are retained for quality and safety monitoring for 90 days by default; customers can opt-out of downstream quality retention via account settings or contract.
- KV cache remains in-memory to serve the session and is not written to durable storage unless the customer explicitly requests snapshot export.
- Erasure requests: standard workflow is a verified request via the customer portal or signed support ticket; we provide deletion confirmation (timestamp + artifact ids purged) within 5 business days for standard hosted accounts; accelerated evidence (audit logs/SHA identifiers) is available under enterprise contracts.

Operational detail (for your audit):
1) Streaming tokens / partial responses:
   - Transient buffers exist in-process on serving nodes to enable low-latency streaming.
   - By default these buffers are not written to any persistent store. If a route is configured to persist streaming transcripts (rare; customer opt-in), they are written to an isolated retention bucket with the same retention profile as finalized requests.

2) Prompts (customer-sent inputs):
   - A prompt is recorded as a request record once the API call completes (or the client indicates completion).
   - Default retention for request records: 30 days (hosted). Requests are indexed for routing/diagnostics but access is strictly logged.

3) Model-generated outputs:
   - Final responses are stored as "derived artifacts" for 90 days by default to support safety/quality investigations and regression detection.
   - Customers can opt out: account-level setting "suppress_quality_retention" prevents copying final responses into the quality store; some features (e.g., safety alerts) may be degraded without retention.

4) KV cache and session state:
   - KV caches are allocated per-session and live in GPU/shared memory. They are never persisted to object storage by default.
   - Snapshots or long-lived session exports are only created when the customer requests them. Those exports are treated as customer-managed artifacts and follow the retention policy chosen at export time.

5) Attachments and binary uploads:
   - Files uploaded as part of requests are stored in a customer-scoped bucket and inherit the request retention timeline unless the customer elects a different bucket policy.

6) Erasure workflow and evidence:
   - Initiation: customer portal request OR signed support ticket with account owner verification.
   - Processing: platform locates artifacts by request id, message id, or hash. Deletion is executed across indexes, backups, and archival stores where applicable.
   - SLA: 5 business days for standard hosted customers; 1 business day for enterprise SLA customers.
   - Evidence: we return a deletion certificate that includes the artifact ids, deletion timestamps, and the set of storage locations purged. For enterprise customers we can provide redacted audit logs and a signed attestation.

I'll attach a compact retention matrix to this thread. If you'd like, we can run through an example erasure for one of your test queries on a short call.

Thanks,

Adding legal/controls clarifications for the auditor:
- Backups: routine snapshot backups are retained for disaster recovery for up to 14 days by default. Backups are logically isolated and included in the erasure sweep when a verified erasure request references affected records; we log the sweep but cannot always provide individualized backup-level proof unless under enterprise support.
- Residency: for EU-bound customers we ensure that request and derived artifacts are stored in-region by default when the account is configured for EU residency. Deletion follows the same workflows but may require additional cross-region coordination for replicated artifacts.
- Compliance artifacts: we can supply redacted manifests showing deletion activity (object keys, timestamps) as supporting evidence for auditors. Full raw backups or unredacted logs are only shared under an approved legal/contractual process (e.g., DPA/SoW).

If the BrightBank team wants a tighter default (for example, 7-day request retention and no derived artifact retention), we can propose a configuration and pricing change; I'll put a short proposal together if requested.

- Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
